what_this_is: A view of frozen whole-pipeline ECDLP measurements, curve by curve, each against its own family's matched reference and generic floor. No new measurement.
what_this_is_not: a claim about any curve not on it
unit: none: the board has three families, each with its own unit, reference and floor (families[*].unit, .reference, .floor); S, ratio to reference and ratio to floor are comparable within a family and nowhere else
success_criterion: Every verified, measured improvement over the current index-calculus baseline is a success. Beating Pollard rho is the long-term goal; each row's ratio to the matched rho is the distance remaining, not a pass/fail gate.

A.title: Koblitz, one target
A.unit: one batched affine addition (`add_many` over 1,024 subgroup points), per √r
A.reference: One-target rho on the same point, measured as built (its set-up plus its walk), in the same unit and the same process; its answer replayed and verified (§23; rule v7 at baseline v7).
A.floor: √(π/4n) rho steps per √r: generic, one target, no precomputation, A = 2n by signed Frobenius and negation, n the extension degree. Stated in steps and not rescaled to units, so × floor here divides units by steps.
A.status: primary comparison: one target, as AGENTS.md's one-target rule requires

B.title: Prime and random-binary ladder
B.reference: Matched Pollard rho on the same instance, one target: the negation-map r-adding walk (A = 2), counted in GAE, verified [d]G = Q (§18).
B.floor: √(π/4) ≈ 0.886 GAE per √r: generic, one target, no precomputation, A = 2 usable automorphisms (negation).
B.status: primary comparison: one target per instance

C.title: Koblitz, 32-target batch
C.unit: one batched affine addition (`add_many` over 1,024 subgroup points), per √r, per target
C.reference: Batch rho on the same 32 targets (signed Frobenius and negation), its counted operations priced at the canonical step, one batched addition plus the table canonicalisation, in the same process (§20). Collisions shared across the 32 targets are in its cost per target.
C.floor: L(32)·√(π/4n) steps per √r per target, with L(32) = 0.19869: the one-target floor of table A times Kuhn–Struik's batch share. Stated in steps and not rescaled to units, and a smaller object than table A's floor, so × floor in C and in A do not compare.
C.status: historical diagnostic under AGENTS.md's one-target rule: 32 targets solved together

points.label: Lazy orbit-member index, fully priced (*_full), stride-renew, vs rho-frob: best cell icv1-f2m29-tm40309-30c52b96 (r = 2^15.4)
points.detail: The frozen Frobenius-orbit IC with its pair table's orbit-member index resolved on a hit instead of built for every base point (same table, relations, rank and logarithms: 856/856 run pairs identical). Paired against the fully priced signed-Frobenius rho on 32 targets x 3 rounds per curve: 1.272 [0.770, 1.803] at the best cell (interval includes 1), was 1.566 [0.992, 2.347] with the eager table on other seeds. Against rho-strong the lazy arm is cheaper at n = 13, 17, 19, 29, a tie at n = 31 (0.985 [0.908, 1.062], was 1.221) and above it at n = 23, 37, 41. Eager / lazy 1.12-1.44x on seven curves, 1.014x at n = 41. L0, counts only.

points.label: Two orbit columns under the lazy oracle, fully priced (*_full), stride-renew, vs rho-frob: best cell icv1-f2m29-tm40309-30c52b96 (r = 2^15.4), frozen c = 1
points.detail: The column-count tuning round: c = 2 against the per-curve column count frozen on 2026-10-14, all under the lazy orbit-member oracle, paired against the fully priced signed-Frobenius rho on 32 targets x 3 rounds per curve (n37: 16 x 3). The round's best cell is the frozen c = 1 arm at n = 29 a1: 1.287 [0.971, 1.686] (interval includes 1), a second measurement of the previous point on fresh seeds. c = 2 improves one cell of five: n17 a1, where the frozen c = 1 costs 1.176 [1.063, 1.297] times c = 2 (2.152 -> 1.830 against rho-frob). It is dearer at n13, n23, n29 and n37 (frozen / c = 2 down to 0.246 at n37), so the frozen counts stay the better choice on four of five curves; the n17 gain is a tuning result on these seeds and needs fresh seeds before it is a rule. No exponent change; no ranking against rho is claimed. L0, counts only. Not validated under the 2026-10-19 gate.

points.label: Rule v8: the Koblitz descent at baseline v8 against a matched rho, one target cold, closest size 2^36.6
points.detail: Rule v8: ledger section 23's six sizes (2^36.6-2^47.2, 64 public points and four A/A repeats a size, 408/408 rows checked in each of two runs of one binary) against a matched rho, the signed-Frobenius walk with its canonicalisation batched 16 lanes at a time by GFNI and funnel shifts; the control run, the same binary with rho as at rule v7, reads 3.59-11.56x. With the reusable set-up charged the index calculus costs 4.67-18.07x rho cold: 4.669x [4.34, 5.07] at 2^36.6, 18.07x [15.98, 20.58] at 2^47.2. Rho is still faster at every size. The two rho arms take identical walks on 64/64 targets a size; the index calculus's own online time is the same in both runs (0.976-1.033). The distance to rho is larger than rule v7 reported because rho was unmatched, not because the index calculus slowed; the ln-ln slope is 0.168 (t interval 0.128-0.208; rule v3: 0.176), not distinguishable from v3's. No curve with log2 r >= 50 is runnable by this single-word pipeline. Class: accounting (a corrected reference); the batched rho kernel is engineering; no advance.

points.label: Planner validation (ic-planner/1): plan vs rho.negation, best registered cell icv1-fp24-tm5099-a6f137c6 (r = 2^24.0)
points.detail: ic plan / ic bench --auto (ic-planner/1) checked on six prime curves outside its evidence, each plan against every alternative one change away from it (ecbench, 24 verified runs per arm and curve, audits OK). Best cold one-target cell on a registered curve: icv1-fp24-tm5099-a6f137c6 (log2 r 24.00), S(plan)/S(rho.negation) 14.39 [11.63, 18.45], planner prediction 12.23. Rho is cheaper on all six curves (12.6-25.8x). At w = 0 every alternative costs more than the plan; the doubled base is not separated across the band (below 1 at w = 1). Tooling validation: the plan is the existing best recipe chosen automatically; no advance, no leaderboard row moves.

points.label: Residual collector res2 vs rho.negation, one target cold, best cell icv1-fp36-t454193-44a20818 (r = 2^36.0)
points.detail: Residual collector res2 (ic.pipeline targets=residual, 2-point base, the large-prime limit) against rho.negation on the same 48 one-target workloads, paired ecbench compare; all 512 records of the session verified, audit OK with 12 exact replays. Across the AGENTS.md section 5a band rho is cheaper: res2/rho 2.592 [2.234, 3.008] at w = 0 and 23.29 [20.06, 27.03] at w = 1 (band means at w = 0.1: S 7.926 for res2, 1.248 for rho). Was: the ic plan recipe on the same curve and targets, 40.87 [35.54, 47.01] at w = 0 and 47.25 [40.81, 54.69] at w = 1; res2/plan is 0.063 [0.056, 0.071] at w = 0 and 0.493 [0.433, 0.561] at w = 1, below 1 at every band weight. At r = 2^36.25 (icv1-fp37-t277-91fd6e29): 2.709 [2.336, 3.141] and 24.34 against rho, plan 46.89. The gain is generic: on a curve-free Z/r carrier the collector costs the same (15 of 16 null intervals contain 1), and its exponent is rho's (slope 0.460 for res4 against 0.619 for the plan). Class engineering: S fell for a birthday search on Z/r with a base attached, not an index calculus that uses the curve; no advance. Not validated under the 2026-10-19 gate (no VALIDATION.json), so no leaderboard row moves.

It saves 3.949 s [3.404, 4.494] against same-source K1120/root11 on the matched points (exact sign-flip p=0.000030518). points.detail: Native complete DLPs paired with rho on the same target: 1.24e6x (p = 61), 1.94e6x (p = 41), 3.39e6x and 5.77e6x (p = 31), 5.2e6x (p = 71), all verified; a sixth arm (p = 41, six-point base) stopped at its 10-hour cap at >= 1.5e7x. Rho's unpriced walk work priced at 0, 0.1, 1 GAE: rho ahead at every weight (4.1e5x best at 1 GAE). Trace replay cuts the test 1.74-1.77x (5.85e7 to 3.3e7). points.label: Prime-orbit relation collector, affine eight-orbit candidate vs negation rho, generic 14-bit toy curve
points.detail: The late-main prime-orbit relation collector was admitted to the fail-closed 79-method optimization inventory. On one planted generic a=-3 toy target, the affine eight-orbit candidate costs 5.4169 [3.389, 8.658] times same-target rho.negation_v2 in counted GAE; pricing every uncharged native operation at 0, 0.1 and 1 GAE leaves ratios 5.4169, 5.0235 and 3.0548. Prospective j=0 and j=1728 cross-checks remain 4.2011 and 5.7901 times their cubic/quartic rho references. All 90 records verified and all 72 measured deterministic executions replayed exactly. Factor-base draws remain unpriced, all clocks are L0, each comparison has one workload and four measured pairs, and no ranked leaderboard row or shipped default changes.
